expression_comparison.chosen_because: USDJPY's 3m decline is a counter-trend versus the yield tape. The persistent object is US front-end yields, not USD/JPY spot.

considered_rates.assessment: US 10Y 4.94 is near the 1y 97.8th percentile with a 45.000000000000014bp 3m change; AU 2Y 4.835 sits at the 99.8th 1y percentile while Australian housing is tightening.
US 2s10s is 27.000000000000046bp at the 1.4th 1y percentile, so curve is an executable alternative to spot or outright duration.
CA-US 5Y is -122.00000000000001bp at the 0.2th 1y percentile — a historically extreme cross-market RV object.

considered_spot.assessment: USD spot trend is mixed (JPY weaker-to-stronger over 3m) while UST 2Y trend is one-way into the 99th percentile.

remit: persistent price and macro trends; reject premature fades
stance_summary: The aligned US yield and policy trend is still short UST 2Y; fading it is premature.

evidence_refs: rollup:August CPI keeps the Fed tightening bias intact
trade.invalidation: A decisive break in the US front-end trend or a Fed close-the-door communication.
trade.mispricing: Mean-reversion arguments ignore that the hike is a realized continuation, not a climax signal in the packet.
trade.thesis: Price, revisions and policy are aligned: US 2Y made a 99th-percentile 1y print as the Fed delivered its first hike.
why_now: The cutoff includes both the hike and the extreme front-end percentile.
